Class GameModel

java.lang.Object
model.GameModel
public class GameModel extends Object
Authoritative game state. Owns the players, the board, the row manager and the current phase handler, and is responsible for notifying its registered VirtualViews when the state changes.

Threading contract

After construction, GameModel is mutated primarily by the single game thread owned by GameController. All mutators documented as @CalledOnGameThreadOnly below MUST NOT be invoked from network/handler threads. However, there is one exception: during the ColorChoosingPhase, if the 60-second timeout expires, an asynchronous timeout thread may call notifyChange() to apply random color assignments to inactive players and transition to the SetupPhase. Read-only getters that are accessed across threads (e.g. isGameOver()) are made safe by marking the underlying fields volatile.

    • endGameScoring

      private EndGameScoringDto endGameScoring
      End-game results owned by the model so they survive a reconnection and can be re-sent on demand (see notifyEndGame()).

      endGameScoring is written only on the game thread (in EndOfGamePhase.onEnter, before the DB thread is even started) and is null for the suspension/forfeit case. leaderboard is the only end-game field written off the game thread (by the async DB thread): it is published as a single immutable GameModel.LeaderboardData snapshot through a volatile reference, so a reader sees either null or the fully built snapshot — never a partial state.

      Throws:

    • notifyChange

      public void notifyChange()
      broadcast the updated state to every registered view. Called by the phase handlers after mutating the model.

      It first creates a new GameStateDto. Then send the state to every VirtualView in the list of views. The list is copied to avoid concurrent modification issues if a view is added/removed while iterating.

      The model notify itself the views, avoiding the model to know the controller. These actions are not blocking for server because VirtualView use a separate thread to send dto.

    • notifyEndGame

      public void notifyEndGame()
      Broadcast the end-game payload to every registered view: the (personalised) leaderboard if available, followed by the game-over with the scoring breakdown. Re-sent on reconnection so a returning player rebuilds the final screen. Performs no mutation (reads fields + I/O on a defensive copy of the views), so it is safe to call from the game thread or the async DB thread.
